title: Recover rigid free flight and restore cells at contact
changes: Optional Motion → Rigid free flight keeps the original 32 ball cells visible while one native compound carries them. Connections return before contact.
Measured transfers retain occupied-box geometry, actual mass/inertia, linear/angular momentum and native face rest. Deformation energy and nonrigid velocity refuse collapse.
Glass/oak/iron/ice complete two-second drops after restoration. Glass is slower (52.58 s) and fracture changes; this is an experimental transition, not a realtime fix.
Reference all-cell mode remains default. Post-fracture rigid continuation, repeated contact activation, local stepping and material accuracy are unfinished.
